name: Serotonin (5-HT)
description: Primary indoleamine neurotransmitter synthesized from L-tryptophan by tryptophan hydroxylase. Synthesized in the brainstem dorsal and median raphe nuclei with extensive projections across the neuraxis controlling affect, satiety, sexual function, and impulse control.

receptorSubtypes.name: 5-HT1A
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Anxiolysis, antidepressant action, autoreceptor somatodendritic inhibition

receptorSubtypes.name: 5-HT1D
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Inhibits 5-HT release, vascular tone regulation

receptorSubtypes.name: 5-HT2A
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Target of SGA antagonism (reduces EPS, increases frontal DA), psychedelic hallucination target
receptorSubtypes.brainLocations: Neocortex Layer V, Basal Ganglia, Platelets

receptorSubtypes.name: 5-HT2C
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Appetite suppression, DA/NE tonic inhibition in PFC. Antagonism promotes weight gain but enhances DA/NE

receptorSubtypes.name: 5-HT3
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Chemoreceptor trigger zone nausea, GI motility, anxiety modulation

receptorSubtypes.name: 5-HT7
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Circadian rhythm pacing, sleep architecture, cognition, antidepressant synergy

majorPathways: Median raphe to Limbic system (anxiety/fear tone)

name: Dopamine (DA)
description: Catecholamine derived from L-tyrosine via tyrosine hydroxylase and DOPA decarboxylase. Controls reward reinforcement, volition, movement coordination, neuroendocrine prolactin suppression, and working memory gating.

receptorSubtypes.name: D1
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Enhances cortical signal-to-noise ratio, cognitive throughput

receptorSubtypes.name: D2
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Target of all approved antipsychotics; >65% blockade needed for antipsychotic effect, >80% causes EPS

receptorSubtypes.name: D3
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Motivation, mood, addiction vulnerability, partial agonism promotes drive

receptorSubtypes.name: D4
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Novelty seeking, attention, highly bound by clozapine

receptorSubtypes.name: D5
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Cognitive modulation and synaptic plasticity

name: Norepinephrine (NE)
description: Central catecholamine synthesized from dopamine by dopamine beta-hydroxylase. The locus coeruleus contains >50% of brain noradrenergic neurons, maintaining alertness, cardiovascular tone, stress responsiveness, and cognitive focus.

receptorSubtypes.name: Alpha-1
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Sympathetic arousal; blockade causes orthostatic hypotension, reflex tachycardia, and sedation

receptorSubtypes.name: Alpha-2A
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Inhibits NE release; post-synaptic stimulation in PFC improves working memory and ADHD symptoms

receptorSubtypes.name: Beta-1
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Heart rate, inotropy; central arousal and tremors

receptorSubtypes.name: Beta-2
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Peripheral bronchodilation, somatic anxiety symptoms

majorPathways: Locus coeruleus ascending to Frontal Cortex (attention & focus)
Locus coeruleus to Limbic structures (panic, trauma recall)

name: GABA (Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid)
description: Chief inhibitory neurotransmitter of the vertebrate central nervous system, synthesized from glutamate via glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD). Maintains neural inhibition and prevents excitotoxic or seizure activity.

receptorSubtypes.name: GABA-A
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Rapid hyperpolarization; positive allosteric site for Benzodiazepines, Barbiturates, Z-drugs

receptorSubtypes.name: GABA-B
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Slow, prolonged inhibitory tone; activates inward rectifying K+ channels, reduces presynaptic Ca2+

majorPathways: Local cortical interneurons (chandelier and basket cells maintaining gamma oscillations)
Striatal medium spiny neurons to Globus Pallidus
Purkinje cells to deep cerebellar nuclei

name: Glutamate (Glu)
description: Principal excitatory neurotransmitter in the mammalian brain, present in >50% of central synapses. Crucial for long-term potentiation (LTP), synaptic plasticity, and network synchrony, but excessive levels cause neurotoxicity.

receptorSubtypes.name: NMDA (GluN1/2)
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Synaptic plasticity, memory formation, target of ketamine antagonism

receptorSubtypes.name: AMPA (GluA1-4)
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Fast basal excitatory transmission, AMPA throughput elevation key to rapid ketamine antidepressant effects

receptorSubtypes.name: mGluR1-8
receptorSubtypes.mechanism: G-protein coupled (Group I Gq, Group II/III Gi)
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Presynaptic autoinhibition and modulatory tuning of excitatory tone

name: Acetylcholine (ACh)
description: Synthesized from choline and acetyl-CoA by choline acetyltransferase (ChAT). Mediates cortical arousal, attention, encoding of new memories, and autonomic parasympathetic outflow.

receptorSubtypes.name: M1 (Muscarinic)
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Cognition, memory, salivary/lacrimal secretion. Antagonism causes memory blur, dry mouth, constipation

receptorSubtypes.name: M2/M4
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Autoreceptor feedback and striatal modulation

receptorSubtypes.name: Alpha-4-Beta-2 Nicotinic
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: DA release in NAcc, attention, nicotine dependence target

receptorSubtypes.name: Alpha-7 Nicotinic
receptorSubtypes.primaryFunction: Sensory gating, auditory P50 filtering deficits in schizophrenia

majorPathways: Nucleus Basalis of Meynert to widespread Neocortex
Septal nuclei to Hippocampus (theta rhythm generation)
